sizing.entry: 2 tranches over ~6 weeks: half now, half after the Oct 27-30 hyperscaler capex guides and the ~Nov 17 Q3 FY27 print
sizing.overlap: AVGO (same AI-accelerator and hyperscaler-capex driver; a direct competitor for the same budgets), GOOGL (a top customer whose capex is NVDA revenue and whose TPU competes), VST (AI data-center power, same capex cycle). About $1.46k of ~$2.34k invested already rides AI capex.
sizing.reason: Fact-checks found no thesis problem, and compression is mostly priced in (19.5x NTM at the 10-05 base; 15.09x calendar NTM at the 2026-10-23 close, 14.80x ex-SBC). But the downside scenario (2027-28 capex digestion with an EPS cut to ~12x) hits AVGO, GOOGL and VST at the same time, so ~5% (~$500) caps the AI-capex cluster at about a fifth of the portfolio. Liquidity is unlimited and there are no lock-up or listing issues. Event risk is concentrated in late October and mid-November, hence the staged entry. P(Sharpe beats SPY) is 0.47: an expected ~+11% at the 10-05 spot (now +29.6% to the 273.45 research target (12m) at the 10-23 close of 210.96: 273.45 / 210.96 - 1; the 262.70 quoted earlier was the 2026-10-27 set) at 38% vol gives a Sharpe of ~0.18-0.2, about the same as SPY's, so there is no clear edge. The 0.47 Sharpe-beat probability and the "low" label are the 10-05 base round's and were not re-scored in this peer-refresh update; sizing itself runs on the combined distribution (allocate.py), not on this text.
sizing.conviction_label_reason: Old scale. The Sharpe-beat probability of 0.47 is essentially no edge. Round-2 checks confirmed the fundamentals but added nothing that raises expected return, the ladder is unchanged from the agents' mean, and the AI-capex overlap with AVGO, GOOGL and VST adds concentration rather than diversification.
